title: Is it a cup or a bowl?

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: What do you do in your free time? Guess: who in this episode has forty-three of the same thing — Leyla or Sam?

chapters.title: Leyla's first cup
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 1 SCENE: a bright pottery studio on a Saturday morning, a woman with round glasses and a lavender apron at a pottery wheel with clay on her cheek, smiling, shelves full of uneven handmade cups and bowls

chapters.title: Forty-three shirts
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 2 SCENE: an open wardrobe completely full of colourful old football shirts on hangers, a red-haired bearded man proudly showing them, a box of normal clothes pushed under the bed

chapters.title: Twenty minutes a day
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 3 SCENE: a calm evening scene split into small moments: someone painting a small picture, someone playing a guitar, someone knitting, all at a kitchen table with a small clock showing twenty minutes

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is hobbies. And Leyla has something to show me.
[laugh] Yes! Look at this cup. I made it myself.
Wow. It's very… round. Is it a cup or a bowl?
It's a cup! I'm a beginner. I started a pottery class two months ago.
Why pottery?
After work I only looked at my phone to kill time. I wanted to get into something new — something with my hands.
And now?
Now I'm completely hooked. Every Saturday morning I'm at the studio, with clay on my face.
[chuckle] It's a good creative outlet. Your job is all spreadsheets.
Exactly. My brain needs a break. What about you, Sam? What's your favourite pastime?
I collect old football shirts. I have forty-three.
Forty-three! Where do you keep them?
In my wardrobe. My normal clothes live in a box under the bed now.
[laugh] That's dedicated. How did it start?
My dad gave me his shirt from 1994. Then I found one at a market, and then another one… and another one.
I think many people want to pick up a hobby, but they say they don't have time.
True. But leisure time doesn't have to be long. Twenty minutes a day is enough.
And a hobby builds a new skill set. My hands are much more patient now. So am I.
And my hands are very good at… folding shirts.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what hobby would you like to start — and what is stopping you?
Mine is pottery. Leyla, you can teach me. See you next time!
Bye for now!
